title: The Nucleus
description: Necrosis attacks the brain of the cell itself. Defend the nucleus — the control centre — to earn a key piece of the Cell of Life.

content.value: Near the centre of most cells sits a rounded structure called the NUCLEUS. It is the CONTROL CENTRE of the cell — the 'brain' that directs all the cell's activities, including growth and reproduction.
The nucleus is separated from the cytoplasm by a NUCLEAR MEMBRANE. Inside it is a smaller round body called the NUCLEOLUS, and thread-like structures that carry the cell's instructions.

NUCLEUS = the cell's control centre / brain
🧫  nuclear membrane → surrounds the nucleus
⚪  nucleolus        → small round body inside
🧬  chromosomes      → carry instructions (genes)

In most cells the nucleus is neatly wrapped in a nuclear membrane — these are called EUKARYOTIC cells (like plant and animal cells). But in some simple organisms like bacteria, the nuclear material is NOT enclosed in a membrane — these are PROKARYOTIC cells. So bacteria have genetic material but no proper, membrane-bound nucleus.
Easy way to remember: EUkaryotes have a 'true' nucleus with a membrane (EU = true). PROkaryotes (like bacteria) have no membrane-bound nucleus.

Key Takeaway: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell, wrapped in a nuclear membrane and containing the nucleolus and chromosomes. Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus; prokaryotic cells (bacteria) do not.

quiz.question: The nucleus is best described as the cell's…
quiz.explain: The nucleus directs all the cell's activities, so it is the control centre.

quiz.question: A cell WITH a proper membrane-bound nucleus is called…
quiz.explain: Eukaryotic cells (plant, animal) have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

quiz.question: Bacteria are prokaryotic, which means their nuclear material is…
options: NOT enclosed in a nuclear membrane
quiz.explain: Prokaryotic cells have genetic material but it is not enclosed in a membrane-bound nucleus.
